essays.q: Distinguish a keyboard from a word-processing program in system classification.
essays.answer: Physical equipment is tangible. A word-processing program is a set of instructions rather than another physical keyboard.

essays.q: A word-processing application is installed. Which category does it belong to?
essays.answer: Software

essays.q: Explain why installing a program is not the same as adding a physical device.
essays.answer: Installing a program adds instructions or data to storage, not a new physical input device. Hardware executes those instructions.

essays.q: A teacher enters marks and checks the results. Which system category describes the teacher?
essays.answer: Liveware

essays.q: Explain one responsibility of a user in producing accurate results.
essays.answer: People choose tasks, enter accurate data and interpret output. The system does not remove human responsibility for mistakes.
Equipment sending data or instructions into a computer

essays.q: A scanner captures a drawing for a computer. Which role is it performing?
essays.answer: Input device

essays.q: Trace a scanned drawing through input, processing and output.
essays.answer: It sends a digital representation inward. The image may then be processed, displayed and saved.
Equipment presenting information from a computer

essays.q: A completed graph is displayed to the class. Which device role presents the result?
essays.answer: Output device

essays.q: Name two output forms for the graph and suitable devices.
essays.answer: A monitor or projector presents visual output; a printer can present the same graph as hard copy.
Keeping files and programs for future use

essays.q: Pupil records must be reopened next term. Which system function is required?
essays.answer: Storage

essays.q: Explain the difference between saving and backing up school records.
essays.answer: Saving retains the working file; a separate backup supports recovery if that copy is lost. Sensitive records also need access controls.

essays.q: A museum describes an early electronic computer built with tubes that used substantial space and power. Which technology is described?
essays.answer: Vacuum tubes

essays.q: Explain two practical disadvantages compared with later designs.
essays.answer: Many early computers using this technology were large, produced substantial heat and required more power than later transistor designs.
Electronic components associated with the second generation, replacing many tube functions

essays.q: A timeline shows smaller switching components replacing vacuum tubes. Which technology marks the change?
essays.answer: Transistors

essays.q: Explain why this replacement was important.
essays.answer: These components were smaller and generally used less power than tubes, supporting improved size and reliability.
Many electronic components combined on a small chip, associated with the third generation

essays.q: A timeline moves from separate transistors to many components on one chip. Which technology follows?
essays.answer: Integrated circuits

essays.q: Explain how combining components on chips can reduce computer size.
essays.answer: Combining components reduces space and supports more complex circuits. A microprocessor is a particular highly integrated processor, not every circuit chip.
A processor implementing CPU functions on an integrated-circuit chip

essays.q: A timeline links personal computers with CPU-on-a-chip technology. What is it?
essays.answer: Microprocessor

essays.q: Explain how this technology helped personal computers develop.
essays.answer: Integration helped make smaller, affordable general-purpose systems possible. Modern devices still differ in power and purpose.
